data.why: The repository ships dozens of small JSON configs under test/data/EquationGenerator_configs that are exactly the file format the app's sidebar file-uploader accepts, covering a plain CSTR, a general rate model with kinetic binding, one with rapid-equilibrium binding, and a crystallization model.

goals: Configure a packed-bed chromatography column model (geometry, particle structure, binding, reactions) and read off the resulting governing transport equations in LaTeX form.
Upload a previously saved configuration (JSON) or an existing CADET simulation file (H5) and inspect which equations that setup corresponds to.
Toggle model assumptions and the symbol table on/off to check which simplifying assumptions and parameter units underlie a given equation set.
Switch between unit systems (SI vs. others) and variable naming conventions (CADET vs. legacy) to match the convention used in a manuscript or simulation file.
Export the derived model as a LaTeX/PDF document, a CADET-Python unit-operation template, or a JSON configuration file to reuse in CADET-Core simulations.
Explore a crystallization population-balance model (nucleation, growth, aggregation, fragmentation) in the same way as the chromatography column models.

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose exactly: compose a chromatography (or crystallization) model and get its LaTeX equations, assumptions, symbols and exports. All ten screens I opened support their nodes, and the features are well cut. It needs a light fix before filing: drop the troubleshooting actions, add the H5 import and geometry/binding-mode choices the repo plainly supports, and correct the model-dependent template label.
